OOS_protocol.data_window: to be fixed in the registration before any data is read
OOS_protocol.train_test_boundary: later orders only; the timeout/offset grid is frozen first

capacity_model.note: execution layer; capacity is the host strategy's

counterparty: takers crossing our resting order; the fill-conditioned drift is the cost
drawdown_model: implementation shortfall distribution vs immediate-cross benchmark; not measured
economic_mechanism: Counterparty: the taker who crosses against our resting order pays the spread; we pay in opportunity cost when price runs away and in adverse selection when we are filled just before it moves. An execution-cost saving, not an alpha: it can only improve another strategy's net edge, and the saving shrinks to nothing when fill-conditional price drift is adverse.
eligibility_rules: only attached to an upstream strategy that already has a counted net edge
entry: post-only at touch with a registered re-quote and give-up rule
execution_model: post-only limit with a timeout-cross fallback
hypothesis: Working entries/exits passively (post-only) instead of crossing saves more in avoided spread and fees than it loses in missed or adverse fills.
prospective_protocol: paired comparison on testnet mechanics then owner-account fills, same decisions executed both ways
rejection_conditions: no measured fill outcomes exist for passive orders
implementation shortfall vs immediate-cross benchmark not lower after counting unfilled orders as cost
benefit disappears when unfilled orders are charged the subsequent price move
net saving after measured fees not positive

required_data.gap: testnet mechanics evidence only; no measured passive-fill history
required_data.name: order-by-order outcomes at the venue: fills, cancels, timestamps, fees
concurrent L2 book/trades for the same windows
maker/taker fee as charged to the account

risk_model: missed fills leave the host strategy unhedged; the fallback cross may be at a worse price than crossing at once
status_note: SPECIFICATION ONLY. Nothing has been tested; this is not a winner. bias_declarations state what the protocol must rule out before any evidence counts, not that it has been ruled out.
